Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestAccountingChronology_test_with_TemporalField_unsupported.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestAccountingChronology/TestAccountingChronology_test_with_TemporalField_unsupported.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The original test contains a large amount of dead code: many `data_*` provider methods and dozens of imports that the single executed test never touches. The only `@Test` method calls `INSTANCE.date(2012, 6, 28).with(MINUTE_OF_DAY, 0)` and expects an `UnsupportedTemporalTypeException`. Let me write a focused, readable version.Compilation succeeded. I refactored the test by removing all dead code — eight unused `data_*` provider methods and ~40 unused imports that the single executed test never referenced — keeping only the `INSTANCE` builder (now formatted across lines for readability) and the lone `@Test`, plus a Javadoc explaining the intent. Runtime behavior is unchanged: `INSTANCE.date(2012, 6, 28).with(MINUTE_OF_DAY, 0)` is still asserted to throw `UnsupportedTemporalTypeException`.
